lines.text: God gives a man riches, wealth, and honor but does not let him enjoy them, so a stranger does.
A man with a hundred children and long life, if unsatisfied and unburied, has a stillborn child better off.
The stillborn child never sees the sun, yet has more joy than a man who fails to enjoy his prosperity.
All a man's labor is for his mouth, yet his appetite is never satisfied.
The Teacher asks who knows what is good for a man in his few days, passing like a cloud.
